extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, media scholars, and newsroom editors interested in how audience metrics influence news selection
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and values used to evaluate and select news stories in digital newsrooms, emphasizing both traditional news values and newly emergent audience-driven metrics (clicks, shareability, entertainment). Relevant for analyzing newsroom selection behavior and designing editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: negativity is a criterion for news selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among core traditional news values used historically to assess newsworthiness; typically privileges bad or adverse events as more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: stories involving conflict are considered more newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the set of conventional journalistic selection criteria; conflict-driven stories often attract editorial attention and audience interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: events involving elites (powerful people/institutions) are seen as more newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the established dimensions shaping editorial prioritization; interactions or actions by elites increase perceived importance of an item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: stories that can be personalized (focus on individuals) are favored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages selecting items that present human-interest angles or identifiable protagonists, making abstract issues more relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: the size or scale of an event contributes to newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events with large impact, casualties, or broad consequences are privileged in selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: closeness in geographic terms increases news relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local or nearby events are more likely to be selected for coverage than distant ones, all else equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: cultural similarity or relevance influences newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that resonate with a society's cultural frames or shared identities are more likely to be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional (Galtung-Ruge derived) news value: recency and temporal relevance are key to selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fresh, recent events are prioritized; timeliness remains a core editorial criterion even in digital contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital-era addition: shareability is identified as an emerging news value influencing selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study highlights shareability as a new consideration; editors and producers may prioritize stories likely to be shared online. The paper notes that entertainment is the most common value among shared stories ('stories shared by online readers because they are fun').

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital-era addition: entertainment value is increasingly important and is the most common value among shared stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entertainment-oriented stories tend to perform well on sharing metrics and thus can gain editorial priority despite weaker traditional 'hard news' attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted clickability
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit newsworthiness criterion identified: the predicted likelihood that a story will attract clicks is treated as a news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors report 'predicted clickability' as a new news value—newsrooms anticipate which items will generate clicks and use that prediction when selecting stories. Empirically, storylines of most-viewed articles were more likely to receive attention in subsequent reporting (cross-lagged analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: forecasting how likely a story is to be shared by readers influences selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely related to 'shareability' and 'entertainment'; newsrooms may favor items judged likely to propagate via social networks, measured or anticipated by editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience clicks / audience metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Core finding treated as a selection criterion: actual audience clicks and other online metrics affect which stories are selected for follow-up reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence (cross-lagged panel over six months) shows that audience behavior (clicks) leads to coverage follow-ups. Editors may either directly respond to these metrics or allow them to influence prioritization indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-driven topic prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: topics are prioritized based on audience signals rather than solely on editorial norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study finds that newsworthiness in practice is increasingly audience-defined: editors weigh audience signals alongside professional norms when deciding what to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pile-on dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit dynamic: clicked stories spawn follow-ups—momentum effects where high-attention items attract additional coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a propagation mechanism: a most-viewed article's storyline is more likely to receive subsequent reporting, amplifying certain topics due to audience attention rather than editorial primacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension between professional norms and audience metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Normative criterion/constraint: editors perceive use of audience metrics for news selection to conflict with professional journalistic norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews revealed that editors state norms rejecting audience-driven selection even though behavior indicates otherwise. This unresolved tension is a qualitative constraint on how metrics are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid newsworthiness (editorial values + click signals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual criterion: a blended standard where editorial judgments and audience metrics jointly determine newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors propose 'hybrid newsworthiness' as the practical outcome—news selection increasingly reflects both traditional editorial values and audience-defined signals; this hybridization should be acknowledged when evaluating or designing newsroom selection practices.
